Subject: Data retention & deletion SLAs — follow-up + SOC 2 / GDPR questions

Hi Priya / Daniel —

Thanks again for the call this morning — great to learn more about Amaya's use case (real-time clinical notes ingestion + embeddings for search). Per our discussion, I wanted to summarize next steps and clarify the items you flagged around security/compliance and data retention.

Recap / ask list:
- SOC 2: Redwood is currently SOC 2 Type II in progress; we run quarterly audit cycles and expect the current Type II report to be available in Q4 2026. Attached is a high-level SOC 2 overview.
- GDPR / HIPAA: We support data processing agreements and can sign HIPAA BAA for PHI workloads. We also provide region controls and customer-managed keys for private deployments.
- Vendor security questionnaire: I attached the questionnaire you shared (Vendor-Sec-Questionnaire-Amaya.xlsx). Can you confirm which sections you want us to complete first (security controls, backups, incident response)?
- Data retention / deletion SLAs (you asked for clarifications): see notes below and attached SLA draft (data-retention-sla-draft.docx).

Data retention & deletion (summary):
- Live data: customer data stored in our live stores is removed per request — typical propagation to live indexes occurs within 24 hours.
- Backups: full/periodic backups are retained according to configured schedules; default backup retention is 90 days but this is configurable per account.
- Deletion SLA (promised timelines): Redwood supports configurable deletion SLAs. Our standard proposal for Hosted customers is:
  * Soft-delete / logical delete: immediate (0–24 hours) from serving layer.
  * Permanent purge from primary stores: within 30 days of request (depends on retention snapshot windows).
  * Purge from backups: 30–60 days depending on backup window and retention tier — we can negotiate tighter windows for Dedicated/Private plans.
- Logs & audit trails: application logs and request-level audit logs default to 90 days; extended (365 days) available as an add-on for compliance customers.
- Backups & snapshots: backups are immutable snapshots; once a deletion request is issued we flag the object and exclude it from restores; physical removal happens as snapshots age out per retention policy.

Next steps:
1) We will start the vendor questionnaire (Rishi will own technical sections).
2) Rishi to propose a concise SLA matrix (times for live delete, backups, logs) and confirm what we can commit to for Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private.
3) Schedule a 30-min follow-up next week to confirm final SLA language and SOC 2 timing.

I've attached the SOC 2 overview and a draft SLA doc for your review. Rishi — can you take point on the questionnaire and the SLA matrix?

Thanks,

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap and attachments. A few clarifying questions from our security team:

3) Logs & audit trails: can you confirm retention per environment (prod vs staging) and whether audit logs include request-level content or only metadata?

Daniel — thanks for the questions, happy to provide technical details. Below is a concise summary; happy to jump on a call with your infra/security team if helpful.

1) Backups & S3: our current hosted backups are snapshot-based and stored in customer-isolated prefixes (S3 buckets in our control plane). When a deletion request is processed we perform the following:
   - immediate logical delete from the serving layer to prevent future reads (within 0–24 hours);
   - mark related objects in snapshot metadata so they are excluded from any future restore operations;
   - physical object removal from snapshot storage occurs when the snapshot containing the object rolls off per retention policy. For our default 90-day retention, that means full physical removal can take up to 90 days.

2) Faster purge for PHI: we offer an enterprise add-on that accelerates backup purge windows — typical accelerated option is 14–30 days depending on backup cadence and snapshot chaining. For Dedicated/Private deployments we can guarantee 14-day purge windows as part of the contract. We'll include specific language in the SLA draft.

3) Deletion SLA semantics:
   - "Requested delete" = customer API / console deletion request.
   - "Live purge" = data removed from serving and index layers (0–24 hours).
   - "Backup purge" = data physically removed from snapshot storage (configurable, default 90 days, enterprise 14–30 days).

4) Logs / audit trails: default retention for request logs and admin audit logs is 90 days in Hosted. Audit logs include metadata (timestamps, API keys, request ids, user ids). They do not include full request payloads by default (we can enable request-body logging as a paid add-on for debug/archive use cases, but that has obvious privacy implications). Extended retention to 365 days is available as an add-on and included in Dedicated/Private packages.

Action items:
- I'll update the SLA draft to include explicit language for backup purge windows and PHI accelerated option and re-share.
